Social protection

Social protection policies aim to reduce economic insecurity and protect households against shocks. They can include transfers, insurance, pensions, employment programmes, and other forms of public support.

Studying social protection involves examining both coverage and effects. Important questions include who receives benefits, how programmes affect household behaviour, and whether administrative systems successfully reach intended beneficiaries.
